Sprite sheet for a 2D side-view narrative game: ten figures of the same character, painted by hand in watercolour. The first reference image gives the exact layout and the exact poses: ten figures in two rows of five, all at the same scale, the feet of each row on the same baseline. Figures one to eight (in reading order) are a walk cycle to the right in strict side view; figure nine stands still in side view, both feet flat on the ground; figure ten has turned three-quarters towards the viewer. Copy every pose, the positions of both legs and feet, the arms, the parcel and the satchel, and the place and size of each figure exactly from the first reference; only the painting changes. The first reference is a plain 3D render: take only the layout and the poses from it, never its smooth rounded shading or its plastic 3D look. The second reference image only shows the costume, the face and the proportions of the character: do not copy its drawing style, its outlines or its three-view layout. The third reference image shows only the watercolour technique of the game (flat transparent washes with hard pigment rims and granulation on rough paper, as on its paving stones, crates and barrels): paint the figures with exactly this technique, but do not copy any of its content or its brown and violet colours.

Painting technique: traditional transparent watercolour on white cold-pressed paper, simple and flat like a quick hand-painted picture-book sketch. Each costume part one or two flat transparent washes: one flat wash of its local colour and at most one second flat, hard-edged glaze for the shadow side. White paper left visible inside light areas: the lightest parts of the shirt, the white face stripes and the white fur, and small highlights on the cap, the parcel and the satchel stay bare paper. Hard pigment rims at wash edges: every wash ends in a thin, slightly darker line of pigment where it dried; in places a narrow gap of bare paper between two neighbouring washes. A little pigment granulation in the dark grey fur and in the green. No fur texture, no individual hairs, no felt, no knitted or woven texture, no soft rounded 3D shading, no plush, no smooth gradients, no airbrush, no glossy highlights. No pen or ink outlines, no black contour lines, no hatching. The figures are cut out of the painted paper: everything inside each silhouette is fully opaque, and bare paper inside a figure shows as solid warm white paper colour, never as a transparent hole. Clear, readable colours: cap and vest a clear dark green, the shirt pale cream, the scarf red, satchel and parcel warm brown, the fur dark grey-brown and creamy white, the broad black-and-white stripes of the face clearly readable, small dark eyes. Light from the upper left, mid-light values, no backlight, no rim light, no glow around the figure. It must look like a real watercolour painted by hand: not a 3D render, not a digital painting, not gouache, not a plush toy, not a cartoon with outlines.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Each figure isolated on a fully transparent background, with clear empty space between the figures; no ground, no cast shadow, no frame borders, no paper texture around the figures, nothing cut off at the edge of the sheet.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.
